name: George W. Nebinger School
notes: Options thin out after 5th grade. For grades 6–8 the pickup choices are Zhang Sah, Queen & Rook and Butcher’s Sew Shop (Fridays), plus Philly Art Center and Shot Tower through 6th. Fleisher and Mighty Writers are both within a few blocks for children old enough to walk.
The city’s free, city-funded after-school programs do not include one at Nebinger. The nearest are school-based programs at Vare-Washington for its own students.
checkedNoPickup: Christian Street YMCA (1724 Christian St), K–6. Its pickup list does not include Nebinger.
Kids on 12th (204 S 12th St), K–5. Picks up from McCall, Greenfield, ICS, FACTS, Russell Byers and Coppin only.
ZAZZ (1923 Chestnut St), ages 5–12. Guaranteed pickup from Greenfield, ICS and Marian Anderson only.
Philly Music Factory (2100 Chestnut St). Greenfield, ICS and Marian Anderson only. Its sister site MoveMakers at 812 Chestnut does list Nebinger.
Children’s Village (125 N 8th St), ages 5–13, takes CCIS subsidy. No Nebinger pickup is stated. Phone 215-931-0190.

name: William M. Meredith School
dismissalNote: K–2 at 3:15, grades 3–5 at 3:20, grades 6–8 at 3:24
notes: Options thin out after 5th grade. For grades 6–8 the pickup choices are Zhang Sah, Queen & Rook and Butcher’s Sew Shop (Fridays), plus Philly Art Center through 6th. Fleisher is about three blocks away for children old enough to walk.
The city’s free, city-funded after-school programs do not include one at Meredith.
checkedNoPickup: Christian Street YMCA (1724 Christian St), K–6. Its pickup list does not include Meredith.
Kids on 12th (1112 Chestnut St), K–5. Picks up from ICS, McCall, Greenfield, Russell Byers, Coppin and FACTS only.
Beehive at Bok. Its Bok pickup list is Kirkbride, Coppin, Nebinger, Southwark, Jenks and Vare-Washington.
ZAZZ (1923 Chestnut St), ages 5–12. Guaranteed pickup from Greenfield, ICS and Marian Anderson only.

alsoListed.title: Also on the Meredith Home & School list
alsoListed.intro: The Home & School Association names this neighborhood program too (Skilladelphia, also on its list, has a listing above). We haven’t confirmed whether it picks up from Meredith.
items: Philly P.A.C.K. (233 Federal St): theater and dance classes. phillypack.org

name: Fanny Jackson Coppin School
notes: Coppin dismisses earlier than most programs start. Ask each provider what time they collect children.
Options thin out after 5th grade. For grades 6–8 the pickup choices are Zhang Sah, Makom Community and Butcher’s Sew Shop (Fridays), plus Philly Art Center and the two rec centers through 6th.
The city’s free, city-funded after-school programs do not include one at Coppin.
checkedNoPickup: Christian Street YMCA (1724 Christian St), K–6. It is on Coppin’s 2024 sheet, but the Y’s current pickup list does not include Coppin.
The NeighborHub (formerly Old Pine Community Center). Picks up from McCall, Meredith, Nebinger and St. Peter’s only.
Settlement Music School. Escorts from Meredith, McCall and Nebinger only.
Queen & Rook Game Cafe. Its listed pickup schools do not include Coppin.
ZAZZ (1923 Chestnut St), ages 5–12. Guaranteed pickup from Greenfield, ICS and Marian Anderson only.

alsoListed.title: Also on Coppin’s aftercare pickup sheet
alsoListed.intro: Coppin’s own sheet (posted May 2024) also names this one; everything else on it has a listing above.
items: Fitness Alive, 267-702-6043. Its own site says its aftercare is paused, so ask before counting on it.

name: Vare-Washington Elementary School
notes: Vare-Washington has free before and after school care in the building, through the City’s Extended Day, Extended Year program. The school’s 2026–27 page links an online registration form and names the site director, Ms. Lisa Washington of Greater Philadelphia Community Alliance, 267-401-5488.
Dismissal is 2:54 pm, earlier than at most schools nearby. Most outside programs start at 3:30, so ask each one when its staff collect.

For grades 6–8, Zhang Sah takes children through 8th grade and Queen & Rook through age 16. Ask the other programs about older children. Fleisher is about half a mile away for children old enough to walk.
checkedNoPickup: Philly InMovement. Its Queen Village studio picks up from Meredith, Nebinger, McCall and ICS (Wednesdays); its Bok site from Coppin, Southwark and Kirkbride.
Settlement Music School. Escorts from Meredith, Nebinger and McCall only.
The NeighborHub (formerly Old Pine Community Center). Picks up from McCall, Meredith, Nebinger and St. Peter’s only.
Butcher’s Sew Shop Junior. Meredith, Coppin, Nebinger, McCall (Tuesdays and Thursdays) and Southwark (Mondays, Wednesdays and Fridays).
MoveMakers (812 Chestnut St). McCall, Meredith and Nebinger only.
Kids on 12th (1112 Chestnut St), K–5. Picks up from ICS, McCall, Greenfield, Russell Byers, Coppin and FACTS only.
Christian Street YMCA (1724 Christian St). Serves Stanton, ICS and Marian Anderson.
Imagine That Philly. Runs inside Coppin and Nebinger only.

alsoListed.title: Also on the school’s own after-school page
alsoListed.intro: The school’s 2026–27 after-school page describes this program and lists other options nearby.
items: Other aftercare options in South Philly, as the page lists them: Zhang Sah, Philly Art Center, Mister John’s Music, Sunshine Camp, The Rock School, CoCo Academy, Code Ninjas, InMovement, Queen and Rook, YCCA, Settlement Music, Beehive at Bok, The Dandelion Project, Action Karate (winter and spring break camps), Old Pine Community Center and Tiny Towne Academy (Pre-K families only). The page doesn’t say which of these pick up from the school; the ones whose own pages name Vare-Washington are listed above.

name: Edwin M. Stanton School
dismissalNote: the school’s page gives dismissal as 3:30–3:39 and admission as 8:55–9:00
notes: Stanton has free before and after school care in the building, run by Sunrise of Philadelphia. Enrollment is open all year on Sunrise’s site.
The Christian Street YMCA is a short walk west on Christian St, and the Y’s before-and-after-school page lists that branch as serving Stanton, with care from 7 am and until 6 pm.
Beehive’s group at the Ethical Society (1906 Rittenhouse Square) picks up from Stanton, for pre-K to 3rd grade. It has a listing here; Beehive’s site doesn’t give that group’s hours, so ask Beehive.

The school’s partners page also names Marian Anderson Recreation Center (740 S 17th St), Mighty Writers and a homework club at Grace and Peace Community Church, without saying what each offers or when. Ask the office.
checkedNoPickup: Zhang Sah. Its pickup list covers Meredith, Jackson, Christopher Columbus Charter, Nebinger, McCall, ICS, St. Mary, St. Peter’s and Vare-Washington, not Stanton.
The NeighborHub (formerly Old Pine Community Center). Picks up from McCall, Meredith, Nebinger and St. Peter’s only.
Settlement Music School. Escorts from Meredith, Nebinger and McCall only, though the school’s page says more than 80 students take part in Settlement’s orchestra program at Stanton.
Philly Art Center. Its Queen Village after-school pickup list does not include Stanton.
Mighty Writers. No South Philadelphia location near the school; its closest, El Futuro at 1025 S 9th St, is about a mile east.

name: General George A. McCall School
dismissalNote: Kindergarten and bus riders at 3:30, grades 1–2 at 3:35, grades 3–5 at 3:37, grades 6–8 at 3:39, per the school’s 2023 bell schedule
notes: McCall has a free before and after school program in the building, run by Sunrise of Philadelphia. After school runs until 5:30 pm.
Ten outside programs name McCall on their own pickup lists.

Options thin out after 5th grade. Zhang Sah takes children through 8th grade, Queen & Rook through age 16, and Butcher’s Sew Shop through 15 (Tuesdays and Thursdays from McCall). Sunrise takes grades 6–8 too.
checkedNoPickup: Beehive at Bok. Its Bok list is Kirkbride, Coppin, Nebinger, Southwark, Jenks and Vare-Washington; its Rittenhouse list is Marian Anderson, Stanton, Greenfield and ICS.
Makom Community. Picks up from Greenfield, Childs, ICS, Marian Anderson, Stanton, The Philadelphia School, Wild Seeds and Vare-Washington.
ZAZZ (1923 Chestnut St). Greenfield, ICS and Marian Anderson only.
Christian Street YMCA (1724 Christian St). Serves Stanton, ICS and Marian Anderson.
Imagine That Philly. Runs inside Coppin and Nebinger only.

name: Eliza B. Kirkbride School
dismissalNote: the school’s page gives the school day as 9:00 to 3:39 and doesn’t say for which year
notes: Kirkbride has a free after-school program in the building, run by Sunrise of Philadelphia. Sunrise lists no before care at Kirkbride.

Three outside programs name Kirkbride on their own pickup lists: Beehive at Bok, Philly InMovement’s Bok location and Dandelion After School. For Pre-K, Philly InMovement lists a pickup on Monday to Thursday.
The school’s page names its clubs and teams but not their days or times, so ask the office.
checkedNoPickup: Philly Art Center, Queen Village. Its 2026–27 list is McCall, Meredith, Nebinger, Coppin, Southwark, Vare-Washington and Independence Charter.
Butcher’s Sew Shop Junior. Meredith, Coppin, Nebinger, McCall (Tuesdays and Thursdays) and Southwark (Mondays, Wednesdays and Fridays).
Mister John’s Music. Its list is CCCS, Coppin, ICS, Marian Anderson, Meredith, McCall, Nebinger, Stanton and Vare-Washington.

CoCo Academy. Its Bella Vista list is Christopher Columbus Charter, Coppin, ICS, Marian Anderson, Nebinger and Stanton; its Queen Village list is McCall, Meredith, Vare-Washington, St. Mary’s and St. Peter’s.
Makom Community. Picks up from Greenfield, Childs, ICS, Marian Anderson, Stanton, The Philadelphia School, Wild Seeds and Vare-Washington.
Settlement Music School. Escorts from Meredith, Nebinger and McCall only.

name: Southwark School
dismissalNote: 12:30 pm on early-dismissal days, per the school’s page
notes: Southwark has free before and after school care in the building. The school names Sunrise of Philadelphia as its partner, and it is one of the City’s Extended Day, Extended Year schools.
The school’s own page names six outside programs that pick up: East Passyunk Rec Center, Beehive, Butcher’s Sew Shop, the Dandelion Project, Philly Art Center and Philly InMovement.
Beehive and Philly InMovement’s Bok location are in the Bok building, across Mifflin St from the school.
The school lists clubs and teams without days or times. It says intramural sports are before school.
checkedNoPickup: Mister John’s Music. Its list is CCCS, Coppin, ICS, Marian Anderson, Meredith, McCall, Nebinger, Stanton and Vare-Washington.

CoCo Academy. Its Bella Vista list is Christopher Columbus Charter, Coppin, ICS, Marian Anderson, Nebinger and Stanton; its Queen Village list is McCall, Meredith, Vare-Washington, St. Mary’s and St. Peter’s.
Makom Community. Picks up from Greenfield, Childs, ICS, Marian Anderson, Stanton, The Philadelphia School, Wild Seeds and Vare-Washington.
Zhang Sah (530 Bainbridge St). Its list is Meredith, Jackson (now Coppin), “CCS”, Nebinger, McCall, ICS, St. Mary, St. Peter’s and Vare-Washington.
Kids on 12th (1112 Chestnut St), K–5. Picks up from ICS, McCall, Greenfield, Russell Byers, Coppin and FACTS only.
Settlement Music School. Escorts from Meredith, Nebinger and McCall only.

name: Christopher Columbus Charter School
dismissalNote: its handbook says children can’t be collected early after 3:00 pm
notes: This page is for the school’s North building at 916 Christian St, kindergarten to 4th grade. Grades 5–8 are in the South building at 1242 S 13th St, which isn’t covered yet.
The school doesn’t post a dismissal time. Ask the office when the day ends before you plan a pickup.
The school’s 2026–27 handbook says before care is available before 8:00 am at this building, for a charge. It doesn’t mention after care, and the school posts no list of clubs.
Two outside programs name the school on their own pickup lists: CoCo Academy, a block away, and Mister John’s Music, around the corner on 9th St.
checkedNoPickup: Philly Art Center, Queen Village. Its 2026–27 list is McCall, Meredith, Nebinger, Coppin, Southwark, Vare-Washington and Independence Charter.
Philly InMovement. Its Queen Village studio picks up from Meredith, Nebinger, McCall and ICS (Wednesdays); its Bok site from Coppin, Southwark and Kirkbride.
Settlement Music School. Escorts from Meredith, Nebinger and McCall only.
The NeighborHub (formerly Old Pine Community Center). Picks up from McCall, Meredith, Nebinger and St. Peter’s only.
Makom Community. Picks up from Greenfield, Childs, ICS, Marian Anderson, Stanton, The Philadelphia School, Wild Seeds and Vare-Washington.
Kids on 12th (1112 Chestnut St), K–5. Picks up from ICS, McCall, Greenfield, Russell Byers, Coppin and FACTS only.
Christian Street YMCA (1724 Christian St). Serves Stanton, ICS and Marian Anderson.

name: Marian Anderson Neighborhood Academy
dismissalNote: 3:22 pm for grades 6–8
notes: The school’s own site names no aftercare of its own; it points to the City’s free Out-of-School Time programs and lists partners. Ask the office which partners run on site after school, and when.
One more program names Marian Anderson on its own site but isn’t matched here yet: Philly Music Factory (2100 Chestnut St).

name: Anna L. Lingelbach School
notes: The school’s own site says the school day ends promptly at 2:54 pm, that children should not be dropped off before 8:10 am, and that it has no before-care. It names no aftercare of its own.
Lingelbach is the site’s first school in Germantown, added because families asked for it. If you know a program that serves it and isn’t here, send it in and it goes on this page.

name: Henry H. Houston School
notes: The school’s own site says the school day starts at 8:15 am. It doesn’t post a dismissal time or name an after-school program of its own, so ask the office.
Houston is the site’s first school in Mount Airy, added because families asked for it. If you know a program that serves it and isn’t here, send it in and it goes on this page.

name: George W. Childs School
notes: The school’s own site gives the school day as 9:00 am to 3:39 pm, pre-kindergarten through 8th grade. It doesn’t mention aftercare; the City’s after-school program locator lists free before and after school care in the building, run by Greater Philadelphia Community Alliance, for students at the school.
Childs is the site’s first school in Point Breeze, added because families asked for it. If you know a program that serves it and isn’t here, send it in and it goes on this page.

name: Bache-Martin School
dismissalNote: the school’s site posts no bell schedule; its after-school page has clubs starting at 3:00 pm, one at 2:54
notes: The school’s own after-school page lists what runs on site and which programs collect children from the school, and it is the source for everything here. It mentions an aftercare in the cafeteria until 5:30 pm on Soccer Shots days without saying who runs it or how to sign up, so ask the office.
Bache-Martin is the site’s first school in Fairmount, added because families asked for it. If you know a program that serves it and isn’t here, send it in and it goes on this page.

name: Independence Charter School
dismissalNote: the school’s site posts no bell schedule; its own after-school program starts at 3:15 pm, and at 1:30 pm on Wednesdays

days.name: Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Day

notes: ICS runs its own after-school program at the school, the 21st Century Community Learning Center, funded by the Pennsylvania Department of Education. It has a listing here; ask the school how to sign up and whether it costs anything.

ICS keeps its own calendar, and its days off aren’t the District’s: it is open on Veterans Day and on November 16, for instance, and closed on December 11 and March 19 for report card days. The days off on this page come from the ICS calendar; the days-off planner and the list of who’s open go by the District’s, so check a camp’s dates against ICS’s.

Wednesdays are early-dismissal days at ICS, and programs handle them differently. ICS’s own program starts at 1:30 pm that day, Philly InMovement picks up from ICS on Wednesdays only, ZAZZ charges extra for its Wednesday early pickup, and Beehive doesn’t pick up on ICS’s half-day Wednesdays. Ask each program how Wednesdays work.
If you know a program that serves ICS and isn’t here, send it in and it goes on this page.

name: Albert M. Greenfield School
dismissalNote: the school day is 8:21 am to 3:00 pm; Beacon and Yous both collect children at 2:50
notes: Greenfield’s own site names the programs that pick up at the school: Martial Posture, Move Makers, Evolve Dance, Philly Dance Fitness (its kids’ program is ZAZZ), Makom, Philly Arts Center, Kids on 12th and Beacon. Each has a listing here.
Several programs need a minimum number of children from one school (ZAZZ and Makom need four), and several don’t pick up on half days. Ask before counting on a half day.
If you know a program that serves Greenfield and isn’t here, send it in and it goes on this page.

alsoListed.title: Also on the Greenfield Home & School list
alsoListed.intro: The Home & School Association’s list of after-school programs names these too. It says they are unaffiliated with the school, and we haven’t confirmed Greenfield pickup on their own pages.
items: BZBI Neziner Hebrew School (300 S 18th St): Wednesdays 4:00–6:00 pm for K–7th grade. BZBI’s own page offers a 3:00 pm pre-care with pickup from participating schools without naming them; the Home & School list says Greenfield is one. bzbi.org
After School Philly (2210 Walnut St), which the list describes as working with MoveMakers Philly, Martial Posture and Philly Music Factory. afterschoolphilly.com

name: Jenks Academy for the Arts and Sciences
aliases: Jenks Academy for Arts and Sciences
Jenks Academy for the Arts & Sciences
dismissalNote: the school day is 7:30 am to 2:09 pm, earlier than at most schools
notes: Jenks’s own site names no after-school program of its own. It lists clubs and activities, among them chess, debate, Girls on the Run, Body Empowerment and elementary intramural sports, without saying when they meet, so ask the office which run after dismissal.

School ends at 2:09 pm. Two Mount Airy programs name Jenks on their pickup lists, Zhang Sah and Philly Art Center; ask each what time they collect children and how they handle half days, when Jenks lets out earlier still.
If you know a program that serves J.S. Jenks and isn’t here, send it in and it goes on this page.

name: Russell Byers Charter School
dismissalNote: 7th and 8th graders who ride SEPTA leave at 3:20, and the handbook asks families to collect children by 4:00 pm

days.name: Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Day

notes: Russell Byers’s 2026–27 Parent & Guardian Handbook mentions an RBCS After School Program at the school, but the site gives no hours, grades or cost for it. It has a listing here; ask the office how it works and how to sign up.

Byers keeps its own calendar, and its days off aren’t the District’s: it is closed for interim conferences on October 8 and December 21, on March 10 for Eid al-Fitr and on May 17 for Eid al-Adha, for instance, and its last day is June 3. The days off on this page come from the Byers calendar; the days-off planner and the list of who’s open go by the District’s, so check a camp’s dates against Byers’s.
Kids on 12th picks up from Byers. Ask how it handles Byers’s own days off and early dismissals, which aren’t the District’s.
If you know a program that serves Russell Byers and isn’t here, send it in and it goes on this page.

alsoListed.title: Also named for Russell Byers elsewhere
alsoListed.intro: A third-party roundup of after-school pickup lists names this program for Byers too, but its own pages don’t.
items: Philly Art Center (2333 Fairmount Ave and other studios): the roundup lists Russell Byers Charter among its pickup schools, but the art center’s own pickup lists name only Bache-Martin, Greenfield, St. Francis Xavier and Independence Charter for Fairmount. phillyartcenter.com

name: Cook-Wissahickon School
dismissalNote: the school day is 8:50 am to 3:29 pm
notes: Cook-Wissahickon’s own site names one after-school partner, the Urban Youth Afterschool Program (Urban Youth King & Queens, or UYKQ), which runs before and after care in the building. It has a listing here.
The clubs the school’s site lists (robotics, intramural sports, volleyball, art club, yearbook) are described as running during the school day, so they aren’t listed here as after-school care.
UYKQ runs on early-dismissal days but not when the school closes early for weather. Ask Zhang Sah, which also picks up here, how it handles half days.
If you know a program that serves Cook-Wissahickon and isn’t here, send it in and it goes on this page.

name: Robert Morris School
dismissalNote: the school’s bell schedule page is empty; its after-school clubs start at 3:45 pm and the Caring People Alliance program at 3:30 pm
notes: Two things run in the building after school. Caring People Alliance runs a free after-school program there, Monday to Friday until 6:00 pm, for Morris students only; it is listed in the City’s program locator. The school runs its own clubs too: tech, music, volleyball and writing.
The school doesn’t post a dismissal time, half days or how the after-school program handles early dismissals. Ask the office.
If you know a program that serves Robert Morris and isn’t here, send it in and it goes on this page.

name: Charles W. Henry School
dismissalNote: the school day is 8:45 am to 3:24 pm
notes: Henry’s own site names Urban Youth King and Queens (UYKQ) among its community partners; UYKQ runs before and after care in the building and has a listing here. Philly Art Center’s Mount Airy studio is a block away on Carpenter Lane, and it and Zhang Sah both name Henry on their pickup lists.

The school’s site lists clubs and activities too, among them debate, robotics, chess, yoga, cooking, Students Run Philly Style and the spring musical, without saying when they meet. It links an up-to-date list; ask the office which run after dismissal.
If you know a program that serves C.W. Henry and isn’t here, send it in and it goes on this page.

name: Mastery Charter School: Thomas Elementary
dismissalNote: the school day is 8:00 am to 3:15 pm
notes: Thomas Elementary’s own page says it offers aftercare through two providers, Mastermindz and SafeHaven, from dismissal to 6:00 pm, Monday to Friday. It says SafeHaven is free and Mastermindz accepts childcare subsidies. Neither provider has a website we could find, so both listings rest on the school’s page; the school’s page gives a contact number for each.

Thomas follows the Mastery Schools calendar, not the District’s. Its days off on this page come from Mastery’s 2026–27 Philadelphia calendar: it closes for Yom Kippur, Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha, and its spring break is March 22 to 26. The days-off planner and the list of who’s open go by the District’s days, so check a camp’s dates against Mastery’s.
Mastery’s calendar marks early dismissals on November 10, December 23, February 9, May 7 and June 11 (the last day). Ask each aftercare provider whether it covers those afternoons.
Thomas Elementary teaches kindergarten to 6th grade; its students can go on to the Mastery Thomas Campus for 7th to 12th grade, which is a separate building at 927 Johnston St.
If you know a program that serves Mastery Thomas and isn’t here, send it in and it goes on this page.

name: Eleanor C. Emlen School
dismissalNote: the school day is 8:15 am to 2:54 pm
notes: Emlen’s own site says the Boys & Girls Club provides after-school and summer programming for its students, and the Boys & Girls Clubs of Philadelphia list Emlen as one of their school sites, for enrolled students. The school also lists an After School Choir and an After School Step Club of its own.
Neither the school nor the club posts the club’s hours or how it handles half days. Ask the office, or the club’s site number on its listing.
If you know a program that serves Emlen and isn’t here, send it in and it goes on this page.

name: Richard R. Wright School
dismissalNote: the school day is 7:30 am to 2:09 pm
notes: Two free programs run in the building after school. LEGACY Youth Tennis and Education runs Champions on the Rise there, part of the City’s Out-of-School Time program, and Shoot Basketballs NOT People runs an after-school program at Wright for 3rd to 5th graders. Wright’s own site describes after-school enrichment but doesn’t name the providers.

Wright is a Community School. Its site says children can’t be picked up for an early dismissal after 1:30 pm, and sends families to its handbook for early dismissals and weather closings. Ask each program what happens on a half day.
If you know a program that serves Wright and isn’t here, send it in and it goes on this page.

name: John B. Kelly School
dismissalNote: the school day is 8:50 am to 3:29 pm
notes: Two programs run in the building. Urban Youth King & Queens (UYKQ) runs after care at Kelly for kindergarten to 3rd grade, and Zhang Sah lists John B. Kelly among its school-based programs. Kelly’s own site names both among its community partners.
Neither UYKQ’s page nor Zhang Sah’s says how half days are handled at Kelly. Ask both programs, and the office, before counting on an early-dismissal afternoon.
If you know a program that serves J.B. Kelly and isn’t here, send it in and it goes on this page.

name: Franklin S. Edmonds School
dismissalNote: the school day is 7:30 am to 2:09 pm
notes: Two programs run in the building, both listed in the City’s program locator. The Indochinese American Council (IAC) runs an after-school program for kindergarten to 8th grade, Monday to Friday until 5:30 pm, and Young Men and Women In Charge (YMWIC) runs a free STEM program for 6th to 8th graders on Tuesdays and Wednesdays. The City’s listing for IAC doesn’t give a cost.
Edmonds’s own site posts its bell schedule but doesn’t mention after school, half days or how the programs handle early dismissals. Ask the office, and each program.
If you know a program that serves Edmonds and isn’t here, send it in and it goes on this page.

name: Frances E. Willard School
dismissalNote: the school’s schedule page gives school hours of 9:00 am to 3:39 pm, and 12:39 pm on early-dismissal days
notes: Two free programs run in the building after school, both part of the City’s Out-of-School Time program: Early Life Academy’s before and after care, and WES Health’s WLCAS group on Monday to Thursday afternoons. Willard’s own site doesn’t mention after school.

Willard’s schedule page says children are dismissed at 12:39 pm on early-dismissal days. Early Life Academy says it follows the District’s closings and holidays; ask it whether it opens early on a half day.

Zhang Sah lists Willard among the schools where it runs its school-based martial arts program, but its site now turns away automated reading, so we couldn’t read it this time. Ask the office whether it runs this year.
If you know a program that serves Willard and isn’t here, send it in and it goes on this page.

alsoListed.title: Also named for Willard
alsoListed.intro: These are named for Willard, but we couldn’t confirm them on the program’s own page this time.
items: Zhang Sah School-Based Programs: Zhang Sah’s after-school page has listed “Francis Willard” among its school-based programs. zhangsah.org

name: Henry C. Lea School
aliases: Henry C. Lea Elementary and Middle School
dismissalNote: the school day is 9:00 am to 3:39 pm
notes: Lea’s own site says the University-Assisted Community School (UACS) After-School Program, from Penn’s Netter Center, runs at the school from 3:30 to 6:00 pm on weekdays, free for Lea students in kindergarten to 8th grade. Its clubs (anime, chess, choir, drama, garden and student council) meet during those hours.
Parent Infant Center’s After School Center, at 4205 Spruce St, says its teachers meet and walk children over from Lea. It takes kindergarten to 4th grade, for a fee.
Lea’s site says families can’t walk children to class, and that a child leaving early is brought to the main office. It sends families to its handbook for early dismissals and weather closings.
If you know a program that serves Lea and isn’t here, send it in and it goes on this page.

name: James Rhoads School
dismissalNote: the principal’s letter for 2025–26 on the school’s site says school starts at 8:10 am and ends at 2:54 pm
notes: To Our Children’s Future with Health runs Safe Haven IV, free before and after care in the building, part of the City’s Extended Day program. Rhoads’s own site names its Safe Haven partnership.
Rebel Arts Movement runs Rebel Tumblers, a free tumbling class, at Rhoads on Monday and Tuesday afternoons.

The principal’s letter on the school’s site, written for 2025–26, also named the Community Council’s Artistic and Cultural Enrichment (A.C.E.) program at Rhoads. The City’s 2026–27 listings show A.C.E. at Locke and Martha Washington instead, so ask the office whether it runs at Rhoads this year.
If you know a program that serves Rhoads and isn’t here, send it in and it goes on this page.

alsoListed.title: Also named by Rhoads
alsoListed.intro: The school’s site names this program, but we couldn’t confirm it for this school year.
items: The Community Council’s Artistic and Cultural Enrichment (A.C.E.) program, named in the principal’s 2025–26 letter as free before and after care. cchss.org

name: Juniata Park Academy
address: 801 E Hunting Park Ave, Philadelphia, PA 19124
dismissalNote: kindergarten to 2nd grade at 2:45 pm, 3rd and 4th at 2:50 pm, and 5th to 8th at 2:54 pm; on half days 11:50 am (11:54 am for 5th to 8th)
notes: Juniata Park’s own site says its after-school program is run by the YMCA. The City lists the YMCA’s free before care (7:00 to 8:30 am) and after school (2:45 to 6:00 pm) at the school for kindergarten to 8th grade.
After-School All-Stars runs a free program at the school on Tuesdays and Thursdays for 5th to 8th graders.
The school’s site also lists clubs (STEAM, robotics, art, Girls on the Run and others) without days or times. Ask the office which run after school.
If you know a program that serves Juniata Park and isn’t here, send it in and it goes on this page.

name: Joseph Greenberg School
dismissalNote: the school’s bell schedule, last updated in 2021, shows homeroom at 7:30 am and dismissal at 2:05 to 2:09 pm
notes: Two free after-school programs run in the building, both part of the City’s Extended Day program: the Boys & Girls Club at Greenberg, which the Boys & Girls Clubs of Philadelphia list as a school extension site for enrolled students, and the Philly KiDZ Initiative. Greenberg’s own site doesn’t describe either one.
Greenberg’s bell schedule page was last updated in 2021. Ask the office for this year’s dismissal time, and ask each program what it does on half days.
If you know a program that serves Greenberg and isn’t here, send it in and it goes on this page.

name: D. Newlin Fell School
dismissalNote: the school’s bell schedule gives a school day of 9:00 am to 3:39 pm, with breakfast from 8:30 am
notes: Greater Philadelphia Community Alliance (GPCA) runs Fell’s after-school program: GPCA’s own page lists Fell among the schools it serves, and Fell names GPCA as a community partner. Girls on the Run also has a team at Fell this fall.
Fell’s page lists clubs, among them art, chess, choir, reading, Scrabble and intramural sports, without saying whether they meet after school. Ask the office which ones run after dismissal.
Fell’s site points to its parent and student handbook for early dismissals. Ask GPCA what it does on half days.
If you know a program that serves Fell and isn’t here, send it in and it goes on this page.

alsoListed.title: Also named by Fell
alsoListed.intro: Fell’s own site names these, but we couldn’t confirm them on the program’s own page this time.
items: ASAP Philly (After-school Activities Program): on Fell’s list of community partners. ASAP’s site turned away our reader, so we couldn’t check which schools it serves. phillyasap.org

name: Alain Locke School
dismissalNote: the school’s site says school starts at 8:45 am and doesn’t post a dismissal time
notes: Community Council’s ACE (Artistic & Cultural Enrichment) after-school program runs at Locke, free, 3:00 to 6:00 pm on weekdays, according to the City’s program locator. Girls on the Run also has a team at Locke this fall.
Locke’s own site is thin: it gives the start of the school day but no dismissal time, after-school page or partners list. Ask the office for the dismissal time and what happens on half days.

Lee Cultural Center, a City rec center about a fifth of a mile east on Haverford Avenue, lists an after-school program for ages 6 to 12. Its listing doesn’t mention picking children up from the school.
If you know a program that serves Locke and isn’t here, send it in and it goes on this page.

name: Richmond School
dismissalNote: the school’s daily schedule gives a school day of 9:00 am to 3:39 pm; before-school clubs may start at 7:45 am, first come, first served, and it says after-school programs end at 4:45 pm
notes: Early Life Academy runs free after care at Richmond: its own page lists the school, and the City’s program locator gives 3:30 to 6:00 pm on weekdays. Richmond’s schedule page says after-school programs end at 4:45 pm, so ask Early Life Academy which time applies. Girls on the Run also has a team at Richmond this fall.
Richmond’s schedule page has a separate half-day lunch schedule. Ask Early Life Academy whether it opens early on half days.
Cohocksink Recreation Center, a City rec center about a fifth of a mile away, lists an after-school program for ages 6 to 13. Its listing doesn’t mention picking children up from the school.
If you know a program that serves Richmond and isn’t here, send it in and it goes on this page.

name: Stephen Girard School
dismissalNote: the school’s bell schedule gives a school day of 8:15 am to 2:45 pm, with breakfast from 7:45 am
notes: The Boys & Girls Clubs of Philadelphia list Stephen Girard as one of their school extension sites, and Girard names the club among its community partners; neither posts the site’s hours. Girls on the Run also has a team at Girard this fall.
Girard’s page lists clubs (Cub Scouts, robotics, math, garden, art, STEM) and intramural sports without saying when they meet. Ask the office which ones run after school.

Two places within about half a mile run after-school programs, though neither says it picks up from Girard: Caring People Alliance’s South Philadelphia Boys & Girls Club on South 15th Street, and DiSilvestro Playground at 15th and Morris.
If you know a program that serves Stephen Girard and isn’t here, send it in and it goes on this page.

alsoListed.title: Also named by Stephen Girard
alsoListed.intro: Girard’s site lists these among its community partners, but we couldn’t confirm an after-school program at the school on the program’s own page or the City’s locator this time.
items: Al-Bustan Seeds of Culture: Arab arts classes. The City’s locator lists Al-Bustan’s after-school program at another school this year, not Girard. albustanseeds.org
Young Chances Foundation: a Grays Ferry youth organization. Its site doesn’t mention Girard. youngchances.org
Rock Reach and Dance Exchange / BalletX: named as partners, with no details on Girard’s site.

name: Thomas Mifflin School
dismissalNote: the school’s bell schedule gives a school day of 9:00 am to 3:39 pm, with breakfast at 8:45 am
notes: The Boys & Girls Clubs of Philadelphia list Mifflin as one of their school extension sites, and Mifflin names the Wissahickon Boys and Girls Club among its partners; neither posts the site’s hours. Girls on the Run also has a team at Mifflin this fall.
Mifflin’s page lists clubs, among them anime, chess, debate, LEGO STEM, Scrabble and a spring musical, without saying when they meet. Ask the office which ones run after school.
No City rec center after-school program is listed within a mile of Mifflin.
If you know a program that serves Mifflin and isn’t here, send it in and it goes on this page.

alsoListed.title: Also named by Mifflin
alsoListed.intro: Mifflin’s own site names these, but we couldn’t confirm them on the program’s own page this time.
items: Philadelphia Youth Basketball: on Mifflin’s list of clubs and activities. PYB’s own site doesn’t name the school; its Sixth Man Center is on Wissahickon Avenue, about a mile away. phillyyouthbasketball.org
